b681712235a3576306cb46d4818b9608a0e0b13d; registration `2026-11-09-build-window-runs.md`) cut
each 16-row window of the build into its runs. Its two CI runs (run 42704879531, attempts 1
and 2; attempt 1's table preserved in comment 6752574723, attempt 2's in 6752208345):

| figure | attempt 1 | attempt 2 |
|---|--:|--:|
| `wikidata` wall, 1 thread | **−1.7% (−2.7, −0.7)** | **−4.0% (−4.8, −3.2)** |
| `wikidata` wall, 2 threads | **−3.5% (−6.5, −0.5)** | **−4.7% (−8.2, −1.0)** |
| `wikidata` wall, 4 threads | −3.3% (−7.5, +1.0) | −0.5% (−2.7, +1.7) |
| `records` wall, 1 thread | **+1.9% (+1.3, +2.5) slower** | **+1.9% (+0.1, +3.7) slower** |
| `records` CPU, 4 threads | +2.2% (−0.8, +5.2) | **+3.8% (+0.8, +6.8) slower** |
| `random` wall, 1 thread | not flagged | **+2.6% (+1.9, +3.2) slower** |
| T-vector build stage (1 thread) | −11.7% | −22.5% |

Its benefit rule was met; its no-harm rule failed (`records` wall at 1 thread flagged slower in
both runs). D075: that head is held, recorded as failed, and never merged; **there is no
reverting to it or re-benching it.** **#310's runs do not count for this head**, neither as
its first run nor as its "other run".

## What cost #310 on high-entropy blocks: two things, not one

`records` and `random` are nearly incompressible. Their windows almost all have 16 runs
(`run_census.rs`, every block of the CI corpora, which are byte-identical to the files counted
here: `records.bz2` SHA-256 `ff8b5f6ed3dd4445…`, `random.bz2` `10d444e6204289af…`, made by
`corpora_gen.py` as `ab gen` makes them, and `bzip2 -9`):

| corpus | windows | 1 run | 2–6 runs | 7–15 runs | 16 runs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `wikidata-independent.bz2` (473 blocks) | 14,735,731 | 83.38% | 10.06% | 5.60% | 0.96% |
| `records` | 599,992 | 0 | 0 | 4.64% | 95.36% |
| `random` | 499,993 | 0 | 0 | 11.03% | 88.97% |

So every window of those blocks takes #310's classifier and then master's one-row steps.
#310's emitted code (`asm/build-old.asm`, rustc 1.99.1, fat LTO, the bench's baseline
x86-64) charges each such window two costs over master's:
1. **The software popcount** (no POPCNT in baseline x86-64): `not`, `or`, `movzwl`, then the
   SWAR count (`shr`, `and 0x5555`, `sub`, two `and 0x33333333`, `add`, `shr 4`, `add`,
   `and 0x0f0f0f0f`, `imul 0x01010101`, `shr 24`), `cmp`, `jbe`: about 19 instructions.
2. **A stack copy of the window's bytes,** which #310's notes did not name. The window's
   16 bytes are in a vector register (`run_heads`), and the one-row steps read `ll[i]` for
   those same bytes, so the compiler took them from the vector: it stored the vector to the
   stack (`movdqa %xmm5,0x10(%rsp)`) and copied each byte to another stack slot (14 `movzbl`
   and 13 `mov`), then each step re-read its byte from there. About 28 instructions a window.
   Master reads the window as two u64s and takes each byte by a shift.

Counted (callgrind, below): #310's build is **+10.0%** instructions on every `records` and
`random` block (+1,406,205 on a 900 kB block: 25 a window), +1.47% to +1.66% of the decode.
That is the size of the 1-thread wall flags (+1.9%, +2.6%).

## The change (code commit b526fdda59a21212dd5c57fd92c0ab279d5c2c37)

Only the classification and the source of the one-row steps' bytes change; the run-by-run
path, its writes, the one-row step and the safety argument are #310's.
- **`run_joins`** returns the window's joins, bit j set when row j equals row j − 1 (j ≥ 1):
  `pmovmskb` of the window against itself shifted by a byte, `and 0xfffe`. A window of one run
  is `joins == 0xfffe`, one of 16 runs is `joins == 0`: **each one compare, with no count.**
  A 16-run window (89–95% of a high-entropy block's) goes straight to the one-row steps.
- **`few_runs`** decides the windows between (2 to 15 runs) as #310 did, `heads.count_ones()
  <= 6` with heads `joins ^ 0xffff`, i.e. at least 10 joins: `POP8[joins & 0xff] + POP8[joins
  >> 8] >= 10`, two loads from a 256-byte static table.
- **`row_byte`** reads row i's byte from `ll` with a volatile read (bounds checked as `ll[i]`),
  in the one-row step, for a run's byte and for a one-run window's byte. The compiler can no
  longer take the byte from the vector, so the stack copy is gone; each byte is one load.

**The emitted classifier** (`asm/build-head.asm`, same toolchain and flags as master's
build in the bench):

```
movdqu (%r14,%rsi,1),%xmm5      ; the window
movdqa %xmm5,%xmm6
pslldq $0x1,%xmm6
pcmpeqb %xmm5,%xmm6
pmovmskb %xmm6,%ebp
and    $0xfffe,%ebp             ; joins (sets ZF)
mov    %r9,0x10(%rsp)           ; a spill of the next window's end
je     <one-row steps>          ; 16 runs
cmp    $0xfffe,%ebp
jne    <few_runs>               ; else: one run, the 16-wide write
...
few_runs:                       ; windows of 2 to 15 runs only
mov %ebp,%eax ; shr $8,%eax ; mov %ebp,%r8d ; and $0xfe,%r8d
lea POP8(%rip),%r10 ; movzbl (%rax,%r10),%eax ; add (%r8,%r10),%al
cmp $0xa,%al ; jb <one-row steps> ; xor $0xffff,%ebp   ; else run by run
```

A 16-run window costs 8 instructions to its branch, against master's 9 (two u64 loads, `mov`,
`xor`, `mov`, `rol`, `xor`, `or`, `jne`). Its one-row step is 14 instructions against master's 15
(the byte is one `movzbl` from `ll`, where master's is `mov` + `shr` from a register): one
more load a row (the row's byte, from the line the window's load just brought in, off the
cursor chain) and one fewer ALU instruction.

**The table's cost:** `POP8` is 256 bytes, four cache lines, read only by windows of 2 to 15
runs (15.7% of Wikidata's, 4.6% and 11.0% of `records`' and `random`'s), two loads each, both
independent of the cursor chain. Four lines of L1D (32 KiB on the runners' 7763 and 9V74) are
negligible against the build's streams; a miss on them costs at most four misses a block.

## Equivalence (required before timing): met

`bwt::tests::few_runs_counts_the_runs` enumerates **all 32,768 masks** `run_joins` can return
(bit 0 clear, bits 1–15 free, none above), and asserts for each (a) `few_runs(joins) ==
(joins ^ 0xffff).count_ones() <= RUNS` and (b) the whole classifier (`== ALL_JOINED`, then
`!= 0 && few_runs`) sends the window where #310's (`heads == 1`, then `count_ones() <=
RUNS`) did: one run, run by run, or one row at a time. It passes (native, release).
`run_joins` itself is checked against a scalar count of runs on every window of Miri's columns
(`miri_inputs_reach_every_window_path`).

## Safety (B5)

- **Miri, native x86-64** (`cargo +nightly miri test --lib -- miri_build miri_inputs`, nightly
  miri 2026-10-26): `miri_build_one_pass` and the new `miri_inputs_reach_every_window_path`
  pass. The second asserts that Miri's columns (`build_inputs(3, 80)`) contain windows of every
  class: one run (the 16-wide write), 2–6 runs (run by run; the near-end fallback is reached
  by the runs that end near their bucket's end, as on #310), 7–15 runs (`few_runs`'s table, then
  one row at a time) and 16 runs (the first compare, then one row at a time). The CI Miri
  job runs both (`--lib -- miri_`).
- **The scalar fallbacks under Miri,** on a target without x86-64's paths
  (`--target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`): `miri_build_one_pass`,
  `miri_inputs_reach_every_window_path`, `one_pass_build_is_the_two_pass_build` (43 columns
  of up to 3,000 rows), `wrong_counts_take_the_two_pass_build` and `run_stores_equal_one_pass`
  all pass: the scalar `run_joins` and `run16` under the interpreter.
- **The test suite** (`cargo test --release`, every target): passes; clippy (all targets) and
  rustfmt clean.
- **The unsafe code:** `row_byte`'s read is of a reference (`&ll[i]`), bounds checked; the
  writes and `set_len` are #310's, unchanged, under the same argument (every slot below n last
  written with its entry; the end check `ftab == lim`).

## Whole decoder: instructions

Inclusive Ir of the driver's `measured` (one `decode_block` on a fresh `Scratch`; driver
`driver_main.rs`, the method of `2026-11-05-deferred-flag-walk/`: rustc 1.99.1, fat LTO,
`codegen-units = 1`). Master is b68171223 (`base-*`), #310 eacd58826 (`old-*`), this
branch b526fdda5 (`head-*`). Profiles in `cg/`. Every output is identical across the three
(`cg/*.stdout`). The walk (`room_segments`) is identical to the instruction in every block.

| block | master | #310 | this branch | build: master → #310 → this (#310 / this vs master) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| wikidata 1 | 19,258,186 | 18,652,955 (−3.14%) | 18,471,069 (**−4.09%**) | 5,250,956 → 4,645,725 → 4,463,839 (−11.5% / −15.0%) |
| wikidata 41 | 18,608,438 | 17,945,838 (−3.56%) | 17,782,493 (**−4.44%**) | 5,103,413 → 4,440,813 → 4,277,468 (−13.0% / −16.2%) |
| wikidata 233 | 19,053,852 | 18,550,694 (−2.64%) | 18,381,004 (**−3.53%**) | 5,038,522 → 4,535,364 → 4,365,674 (−10.0% / −13.4%) |
| wikidata 400 | 18,620,577 | 17,988,122 (−3.40%) | 17,828,095 (**−4.26%**) | 5,026,554 → 4,394,099 → 4,234,072 (−12.6% / −15.8%) |
| wikidata 0 (54 B) | 7,037 | 7,117 | 7,046 (+9) | |
| wikidata 472 (70 B) | 8,252 | 8,357 | 8,262 (+10) | 3,585 → 3,690 → 3,595 |

| records 10 | 63,550,877 | 64,488,682 (+1.48%) | 63,195,465 (**−0.56%**) | 9,342,965 → 10,280,770 → 8,987,553 (+10.0% / −3.8%) |
| random 0 | 84,956,287 | 86,362,492 (+1.66%) | 84,462,266 (**−0.58%**) | 14,008,440 → 15,414,645 → 13,514,419 (+10.0% / −3.5%) |

| block | master: branches, mispredicted | #310 | this branch |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| wikidata 1 | 564,032, 10,485 | 375,929, 15,500 | 431,439, 18,667 |

- **`text`, `pattern`, `runs`, `onebyte`:** no flag slower; `text` and `pattern` at 1 thread

The rule is #310's, with its inherited no-harm policy written out in full.

  the build's tests pass, `few_runs_counts_the_runs` (all 32,768 masks) included.
- **Benefit (required):** on `wikidata` at 1 or 4 threads, the CPU change or the wall change
  excludes zero on the faster side in at least one run, and the same figure's point estimate is
  not slower in the other run (in every other run, if a third is made).
- **No harm (required), as in `2026-11-05-deferred-flag-walk.md`, each run read on its own:**
  - a wall row (any corpus × thread count, all seven corpora) flagged **slower** is a harm
    signal;
  - one more run on the same head settles it: flagged again, it is a harm, and the rule fails;
  - not flagged again, the row is reported as unresolved, with all its runs;
  - at most three runs in all.

  to exclude it.
- **The repeat policy:**

    merge base with master (b681712235a3576306cb46d4818b9608a0e0b13d).
  - **Run 2** is one re-run of that same workflow run (the same head and base), started once
    run 1 has posted its table. Both runs are planned: run 2 is the benefit rule's "other run",
    and it settles any wall row flagged slower in run 1.
  - **Run 3** is made only to settle a wall row flagged slower in run 2 and not in run 1. No
    run is made for any other reason, and none after three.
  - A run whose job fails before the bench produces its table (a setup failure,
    `docs/team/CI-INCIDENTS.md` class B) is re-run as the same run; it is not a run.
  - Each run's whole table is preserved (the bench edits one comment in place) before the next
    run starts.
- **The whole grid is reported:** every corpus × thread count, wall, CPU and peak RSS, the
  resources table and the stage table, in every run, whatever it shows.
- **No retries to pass, no fallback:** if the rule fails, the PR is closed and this entry
  records the negative result. #310's head is not a fallback (D075).
- **Not changed after the data:** the corpora, thread counts, rounds, `RUNS` = 6, this rule.

## What cost #310 on high-entropy blocks: two things, not one

`records` and `random` are nearly incompressible. Their windows almost all have 16 runs
(`run_census.rs`, every block of the CI corpora, which are byte-identical to the files counted
here: `records.bz2` SHA-256 `ff8b5f6ed3dd4445…`, `random.bz2` `10d444e6204289af…`, made by
`corpora_gen.py` as `ab gen` makes them, and `bzip2 -9`):

| corpus | windows | 1 run | 2–6 runs | 7–15 runs | 16 runs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `wikidata-independent.bz2` (473 blocks) | 14,735,731 | 83.38% | 10.06% | 5.60% | 0.96% |
| `records` | 599,992 | 0 | 0 | 4.64% | 95.36% |
| `random` | 499,993 | 0 | 0 | 11.03% | 88.97% |

So every window of those blocks takes #310's classifier and then master's one-row steps.
#310's emitted code (`asm/build-old.asm`, rustc 1.99.1, fat LTO, the bench's baseline
x86-64) charges each such window two costs over master's:
1. **The software popcount** (no POPCNT in baseline x86-64): `not`, `or`, `movzwl`, then the
   SWAR count (`shr`, `and 0x5555`, `sub`, two `and 0x33333333`, `add`, `shr 4`, `add`,
   `and 0x0f0f0f0f`, `imul 0x01010101`, `shr 24`), `cmp`, `jbe`: about 19 instructions.
2. **A stack copy of the window's bytes,** which #310's notes did not name. The window's
   16 bytes are in a vector register (`run_heads`), and the one-row steps read `ll[i]` for
   those same bytes, so the compiler took them from the vector: it stored the vector to the
   stack (`movdqa %xmm5,0x10(%rsp)`) and copied each byte to another stack slot (14 `movzbl`
   and 13 `mov`), then each step re-read its byte from there. About 28 instructions a window.
   Master reads the window as two u64s and takes each byte by a shift.

`random` block (+1,406,205 on a 900 kB block: 25 a window), +1.47% to +1.66% of the decode.
That is the size of the 1-thread wall flags (+1.9%, +2.6%).

## The change (code commit b526fdda59a21212dd5c57fd92c0ab279d5c2c37)

Only the classification and the source of the one-row steps' bytes change; the run-by-run
path, its writes, the one-row step and the safety argument are #310's.
- **`run_joins`** returns the window's joins, bit j set when row j equals row j − 1 (j ≥ 1):
  `pmovmskb` of the window against itself shifted by a byte, `and 0xfffe`. A window of one run
  is `joins == 0xfffe`, one of 16 runs is `joins == 0`: **each one compare, with no count.**
  A 16-run window (89–95% of a high-entropy block's) goes straight to the one-row steps.
- **`few_runs`** decides the windows between (2 to 15 runs) as #310 did, `heads.count_ones()
  <= 6` with heads `joins ^ 0xffff`, i.e. at least 10 joins: `POP8[joins & 0xff] + POP8[joins
  >> 8] >= 10`, two loads from a 256-byte static table.
- **`row_byte`** reads row i's byte from `ll` with a volatile read (bounds checked as `ll[i]`),
  in the one-row step, for a run's byte and for a one-run window's byte. The compiler can no
  longer take the byte from the vector, so the stack copy is gone; each byte is one load.

**The emitted classifier** (`asm/build-head.asm`, same toolchain and flags as master's
build in the bench):

```
movdqu (%r14,%rsi,1),%xmm5      ; the window
movdqa %xmm5,%xmm6
pslldq $0x1,%xmm6
pcmpeqb %xmm5,%xmm6
pmovmskb %xmm6,%ebp
and    $0xfffe,%ebp             ; joins (sets ZF)
mov    %r9,0x10(%rsp)           ; a spill of the next window's end
je     <one-row steps>          ; 16 runs
cmp    $0xfffe,%ebp
jne    <few_runs>               ; else: one run, the 16-wide write
...
few_runs:                       ; windows of 2 to 15 runs only
mov %ebp,%eax ; shr $8,%eax ; mov %ebp,%r8d ; and $0xfe,%r8d
lea POP8(%rip),%r10 ; movzbl (%rax,%r10),%eax ; add (%r8,%r10),%al
cmp $0xa,%al ; jb <one-row steps> ; xor $0xffff,%ebp   ; else run by run
```

A 16-run window costs 8 instructions to its branch, against master's 9 (two u64 loads, `mov`,
`xor`, `mov`, `rol`, `xor`, `or`, `jne`). Its one-row step is 14 instructions against master's 15
(the byte is one `movzbl` from `ll`, where master's is `mov` + `shr` from a register): one
more load a row (the row's byte, from the line the window's load just brought in, off the
cursor chain) and one fewer ALU instruction.

**The table's cost:** `POP8` is 256 bytes, four cache lines, read only by windows of 2 to 15
runs (15.7% of Wikidata's, 4.6% and 11.0% of `records`' and `random`'s), two loads each, both
independent of the cursor chain. Four lines of L1D (32 KiB on the runners' 7763 and 9V74) are
negligible against the build's streams; a miss on them costs at most four misses a block.

# Stewardship of mibz2's production code and releases

This document records who looks after mibz2's production code and releases, what that role
may do without asking, and how a release is carried out and checked. It holds across research
campaigns: a campaign may fail, succeed and finish, or move on to other research, and this
role continues either way. Each campaign keeps its own rules in its own entry document.

## The decision

On 2026-11-04 the maintainer was asked whether the Coordinator's merge and release authority
should be permanent or end with the compact30 campaign. They chose:

> **Permanent steward.** I'm mibz2's standing production and release steward, and compact30 is
> the current campaign under that. A failed experiment stays out of production. A qualified
> improvement doesn't wait indefinitely after passing its gates. Other legitimate maintenance
> isn't held back because of compact30.

The steward is the Coordinator, which is the maintainer's Claude Code session. The role
extended the delegation in the compact30 research charter (§2, report 266) beyond that campaign.
compact30 ended on 2026-11-06. The agent team's standing rules are now `docs/team/RULES.md`
(row A6 is this role).

## The standing objective

The objective is a measurably faster, correct production decoder, properly released. The
steward:
- keeps a failed or unqualified experiment out of production;
- doesn't let a qualified, merged improvement sit unreleased indefinitely;
- doesn't hold other legitimate maintenance back because of a campaign.

## What the steward may do without asking

The steward may open, review and merge pull requests into `master`, and may release, under
these gates.

**Changes that touch measured code** (`src/**`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the bench's inputs)
merge only when all of these hold:
- the tests and parity checks pass;
- CI is green on the head that will merge;
- the CI paired A/B bench (`.github/workflows/bench.yml`) shows an end-to-end improvement
  beyond noise, meaning its 95% interval excludes zero in the beneficial direction;
- no other figure regresses unacceptably.

**Before opening a PR that changes the default decoding kernel,** account for the whole decoder,
not only the part being optimised (RULES.md C4, S2).
- **Count the instructions** executed in `decode_block` on master and on the candidate, split
  into build, walk and the rest. Use matched toolchain, flags and input, and archive the
  profiles. Charge every induced cost: work, memory traffic, synchronisation and control.
- **An excess over master's count needs a stated mechanism,** written down first: what it
  buys (overlap, locality, less contention), its predicted effect at each thread count CI
  measures, and what falsifies it. Falsified, the PR is closed and written up.
- **CI's end-to-end bench decides the merge,** not the count alone.
- **Timing on the shared development machine** is never the evidence. A workstation run is
  evidence only under RULES.md C5.

PR #155 is why: its constructor saved 19.5% of its instructions, its walk added 31%, and CI
measured the decoder 7–19% slower.

**Docs-only and measurement-only changes** merge when CI is green and nothing measured
changed that wasn't meant to.

**A red check** is handled by `docs/team/CI-INCIDENTS.md`. It classifies the failure from its
log, re-runs only the failed job, paced to the outage, and records which checks did not run. It
does not relax the green-head rule above.

**For every merge:**
- merge only the head that CI measured;
- set `expectedHeadSha` to that head;
- a later commit that changes measured code needs a fresh bench.

## Release checkpoints

When accepted production changes have landed on `master`, the steward owns the release:
- Batch changes at sensible milestones. Don't release every research iteration.
- Never release unqualified experimental work.
- Don't leave accepted production improvements indefinitely unreleased.

The release runs through the repository's existing machinery.

1. **Deploy Release** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) is dispatched by hand on `master` with
   `bump` set to patch, minor or major by semver. It runs `just release`
   (`.just/ship.just`), which:
   - bumps the Python and Rust versions together;
   - updates both lockfiles (`Cargo.lock` and `bench/alternatives/Cargo.lock`);
   - writes the crate's changelog with release-plz;
   - commits `chore(release): bump 🐍 -> vX.Y.Z`;
   - tags `py-X.Y.Z`;
   - pushes both the commit and the tag.
2. **The tag alone does not publish anything.** A tag pushed with the workflow's token starts
   no workflow. Deploy Release therefore starts `CI.yml` on the tag itself, by
   `workflow_dispatch`. Creating the tag is not the same as publishing.
3. **CI publishes:**
   - the wheels to PyPI (the `release` job, `pypi` environment);
   - the crate to crates.io through release-plz with Trusted Publishing (the `crates` job,
     `crates-io` environment).

   release-plz also tags `mibz2-vX.Y.Z` and creates the GitHub release.
4. **Verify completion.** All of these must be true before a release counts as done:
   - the CI run on `py-X.Y.Z` succeeded;
   - PyPI lists `mibz2 X.Y.Z`;
   - crates.io lists `mibz2 X.Y.Z`;
   - the GitHub release exists;
   - `CHANGELOG.md` has the version's entry.

   Record the shipped version and its release commit. If any step fails, find the cause and
   reconcile it. A partial publication must not be left unresolved.
5. **Downstream:** bump wikidata-pq's mibz2 pin in a separate PR. That PR follows wikidata-pq's
   own `CLAUDE.md` and must pass its own bench gate. A mibz2 win does not certify a downstream
   gain. A package release is not permission to publish anything to the Hugging Face Hub.

`.github/workflows/tag.yml` is an alternative, for tagging a commit that already carries the
new version. `just ship-rust-and-python` is the local recipe for the same release.

**Identity.** Deploy Release's release commit is made by the workflow's `github-actions[bot]`
identity, as for every prior release. That is the repository's release mechanism, not an
AI-attributed commit. Every other commit is the maintainer's: Louis Maddox
<louismmx@gmail.com>, with no AI attribution in commits, PR bodies, release notes or
metadata.

## What stays with the maintainer

These decisions still need the maintainer:
- relaxing a gate or an acceptance minimum;
- the bench's workload, statistical estimand, repeat policy and merge acceptance rule. Harness
  mechanics and diagnostic instrumentation that leave these unchanged are the steward's
  (RULES.md C6);
- a run on the i9 or another workstation. The maintainer authorises it by running a recipe
  frozen before the run, and that authorises that run only (RULES.md C5);
- new infrastructure, credentials or spending;
- widening the scope beyond mibz2 and its downstream pin bump.

A campaign's rules can reserve more for the maintainer. They cannot give the steward more than
this document and `docs/team/RULES.md` do without the maintainer's own words.

## Standing prohibitions

The steward never:
- reads from, writes to or calls the Hugging Face Hub;
- adds AI attribution;
- changes the allocator;
- weakens the exact checks;
- polls, or sets up cron jobs;
- force-pushes;
- treats silence as approval;
- merges an unbenched head.

## Campaigns

Each campaign has an entry document that maps its charter, roles, protocol, state and evidence.
Read it at the start of a session, after context compaction, and before any consequential
decision. Resolve it to a commit and record the revision that a decision used.

| Campaign | Entry document |
| --- | --- |
| compact30 (ended 2026-11-06, archived) | `docs/journal/compact30-channel/CAMPAIGN.md` (history: `docs/journal/2026-11-06-team-neutral.md`) |

There is no current campaign. The agent team's standing work runs under `docs/team/`.

# mibz2

Publishing a page of the site (a blog post above all): use the `publish-page` skill
(`.claude/skills/publish-page/SKILL.md`).

The team channel (#145) and the role inboxes (#160 Optimiser, #161 Guardian, #162
Researcher, #222 Observer): route every message with `.github/coordination/coord.py`, never from memory.
- **At session start, and every time the coordinator wakes (an event or a check-in):**
  `python3 .github/coordination/coord.py audit` lists any misrouted message, and fails on any not yet in its `RESOLVED` record. This
  is what catches a misroute. The tripwire also records each one live, as a failing `routing
  tripwire` check on #145, but no event from it wakes the coordinator. Correct a misroute, log
  it, then add it to `RESOLVED` with how it was handled.
- **Before posting an assignment:** `coord.py route --to <role> --type CHECKPOINT` gives the
  destination: the role's inbox, or #145 as `TYPE: QUEUED` while the role is busy, or an older
  QUEUED item to dispatch first.
- **After posting:** `coord.py verify --comment-id <id> --to <role> --type <type>` must pass.
  A comment that exists is not a message delivered.
- **Before any merge:** `coord.py head-sha --pr <n> --sha <sha>` must pass, and its SHA is the
  merge's expected head. It passes only for the PR's exact 40-character head, never a prefix.
- **The merge itself:** pass that SHA as `expectedHeadSha`, the merge tool's parameter. The tool
  silently drops a name it doesn't have, such as `sha`, and then nothing checks the head.
- **After the merge:** `coord.py head-sha --pr <n> --sha <sha> --merged` must pass: the PR is
  merged, at exactly that head. A merge call that returned success is not a checked merge.

## A red CI check

Follow [`docs/team/CI-INCIDENTS.md`](docs/team/CI-INCIDENTS.md):
- **Classify each failed job from its log:** A, the change failed; B, setup failed before the
  project ran; C, flaky; D, unexplained.
- **Re-run only the failed job,** paced to the outage. A setup failure blocks only that PR's
  merge, never other work.
- **The green-head gate in `docs/STEWARDSHIP.md` holds.**

## Releases: the coordinator drives them

The coordinator releases mibz2 itself, without asking first, whenever merged work is worth
releasing. **Before any release, read and follow [`docs/RELEASING.md`](docs/RELEASING.md),**
the release runbook. It covers:
- what is worth releasing, and when;
- the checks before a release;
- the release itself and its publication checks;
- the release-scaling run of the current release against the last;
- the CHANGELOG, the downstream bump and the report.

Check what has merged since the last tag after every merge to master, not only when asked.

## Workstation recipes: one tarball back

Every `just` recipe the maintainer runs on their own machine and sends results back from:
- **Writes everything into one new directory per attempt,** never reused (`mkdir`, not
  `mkdir -p`, on a timestamped path), its own console log included:
  `exec > >(tee -a "$DIR/console.log") 2>&1` right after the directory is made. The
  maintainer runs the bare `just` command, with no `| tee`.
- **Ends with `bash bench/bundle.sh "$DIR"`.** It packs the directory into one `DIR.tar.gz`
  beside it, leaving out symbolic links (a shared corpus) and files over 50 MB, and prints the
  path. The maintainer uploads that one file: the chat takes at most 5 files a message.
- **Is given to the maintainer as the git commands to get the branch and the `just` command,**
  nothing else. For a frozen recipe whose run is evidence, the command is
  `just submit <recipe>`. It runs the recipe unchanged, then archives the bundle on the
  `evidence` branch and posts its identity and digest on #145 (RULES C5). Nothing needs uploading. If the
  submission fails, the bundle is kept and `just submit-bundle <tarball>` retries it without a
  rerun. The coordinator reads the bundle from the `evidence` branch at the commit the post
  names, and checks its SHA-256.

**Unattended:** `just submit-when-ready <recipe> <branch>` waits on the workstation for a
`ready/<recipe>` tag on origin. It runs `just submit <recipe>` once at exactly the tagged commit,
then suspends; `hold/<recipe>` stops it. The coordinator sets the tag only once the recipe is
frozen, reviewed and green, through the dispatch-only workflow `.github/workflows/run-signal.yml`
(`signal`: ready, hold or clear), since this session's git proxy refuses tag pushes.
Prepared runs wait in the **workstation queue**, `bench/workstation-queue.txt`
(PROTOCOL.md §9). An entry goes in only once nothing about it remains to be decided. One
command, `just workstation-queue`, runs every ready entry once, then suspends.

`bench-team-size` and `bench-release-scaling` follow it; give any older recipe the same
shape when it is next used.

## The agent team

The team's live machinery is `docs/team/`:
- MODE.md: the register. Reload it at session start and when asked.
- RULES.md: who may decide what.
- PROTOCOL.md: how messages move.
- ROLES.md and the specs.

**ChatGPT Work task prompts** come only from `docs/team/WORK-TASKS.md`. Copy the form and fill in
its placeholders; never draft one fresh.
- **Beside every prompt:** give the task's name, and its model and effort for Louis to select in
  the chat window.
- **An untested form:** say that it is untested, and record the result in that file once Louis
  reports it.

**Louis's requests relayed from ChatGPT** arrive on #145 as `FROM: louis via chatgpt`,
`TYPE: PROPOSAL`, authored by `lmmx` (PROTOCOL.md §7). Act on them only within delegated
authority. Check the interpretation against his verbatim words. Acknowledge each with one
LOG. Anything RULES D reserves still needs him in this session.
Requests to ChatGPT (a re-pin, say) go on #145 as `TO: chatgpt`, `TYPE: CHECKPOINT`; Louis has
it process them. Verify its REVIEW's read-back before acting on it (§7).

Route every message with `.github/coordination/coord.py`, as above. compact30 is history
(`docs/journal/compact30-channel/`, frozen): it is no source of the team's identity, authority
or state.

The Observer (#222) keeps a behind-the-scenes account of what the team is doing and why, on the
orphan branch `observatory/intention`.
- **Dispatching to it:** send it a CHECKPOINT whenever the record moves materially (a result,
  a decision, a merge, a change of direction), one at a time.
- **Correcting it:** correct only major discrepancies, through a CORRECTION, never on wording.
